holidays.name: National Deviled Egg Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble deviled egg, the party-platter staple made by mashing yolks with mayo and mustard, piling them back into egg-white boats, and dusting them with paprika. Devotees are encouraged to make, eat, and argue about the best recipe.
holidays.origin: Like many food days, it is an unofficial observance that grew out of food-lover and social media culture. Deviled eggs themselves go back to ancient Rome, where boiled eggs were served with spicy sauces. The term 'deviled' appeared in English in the 18th century to describe spicy or zesty foods.
holidays.funFact: Deviled eggs are so popular at American holiday gatherings that special trays with 12 or 24 dimples were designed just to carry them without disaster.

holidays.name: Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos)
holidays.description: A colorful Mexican tradition in which families welcome back the spirits of their loved ones with marigolds, candles, sugar skulls, and favorite foods. Despite the name, it is a joyful, affectionate celebration of life and memory rather than a spooky event.
holidays.origin: It blends Indigenous Aztec rituals honoring the dead with the Catholic All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day, which fall on November 1 and 2. The tradition developed in Mexico over centuries and was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2008.
holidays.funFact: Families often build ofrendas (altars) and scatter marigold petals, called cempasúchil, from the graveyard to the home to guide spirits back with their bright color and strong scent.

holidays.name: National Cook for Your Pets Day
holidays.description: A day for pet owners to put on the apron and prepare a homemade meal for their dogs, cats, or other furry companions. It is basically a chance to pretend you run a very exclusive restaurant with a very enthusiastic clientele.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial pet-lovers' observance, popularized through pet-industry and pet-blogging circles. It encourages owners to think about fresh, pet-safe ingredients, usually with a nudge to check with a veterinarian first.
holidays.funFact: Many common human foods like onions, grapes, and chocolate are toxic to pets, so the day is also a good reminder to double-check what is safe before you start cooking.

holidays.name: Look for Circles Day
holidays.description: A day for noticing circles in the world around you, from clocks and wheels to pizzas and manhole covers. Once you start looking, it is almost impossible to stop seeing them.
holidays.origin: This is a whimsical, unofficial observance. The date, 11/2, is sometimes linked to the idea of the number patterns and round shapes in 11/02, as the 0 and the 1s and 2 invite playful shape-spotting.
holidays.funFact: Circles are everywhere in nature too, from ripples in a pond to the pupils of your eyes, and the ancient Greeks considered the circle the most perfect shape.

holidays.name: All Souls' Day
holidays.description: A solemn but meaningful day in the Christian calendar to pray for and remember the souls of the faithful departed. In many countries, people visit cemeteries to clean graves and leave flowers and candles.
holidays.origin: The observance was established by Saint Odilo of Cluny in the year 998 at his monastery, and it spread across the Western Church. It follows All Saints' Day on November 1.
holidays.funFact: In some parts of Europe, bakers made special 'soul cakes' for the occasion, and children went door to door singing for them, which is thought to be an ancestor of trick-or-treating.
